Our proof is the thesis's 55VI argument step for step: conjugate by q and use the C*-identity for 1 -> 2; the p^perp a q a* p^perp = a q a* computation plus a q a* <= a a* <= 1 for 2 -> 3; and the thesis's own 'by a similar reasoning' for 3 -> 1, instantiated by applying the same two lemmas to a*

55XII, definition of an orthogonal set of projections (every two members equal or with product 0), with membership in the projections folded in. The thesis's separate phrase 'projections p and q are orthogonal when pq = 0' has no declaration of its own; it is used unfolded throughout
55XIII part 1, all six equivalents (pq=0, qp=0, pqp=0, p+q<=1, p<=q^perp, p+q a projection). Exercise, no thesis proof

55XIII part 2, first half. The thesis says 'a finite SET of projections p_1,...,p_n is orthogonal', which for a repeated element would make the claim false (the set {p,p} is orthogonal by 55XII yet sum = 2p is not <= 1); ours reads it as a pairwise-orthogonal tuple (Pairwise on Fin n), which is the intended and correct reading. Exercise, no thesis proof
55XIII part 2, second half ('show that, in that case, sum p_i is the least projection above p_1,...,p_n'), as an IsLeast over the projections above every p_i. Exercise, no thesis proof

column6: 56I vna-ceil, the construction for an effect b: existence of a projection p that is the LUB of the iterated square roots, the least projection above b, and commuting with everything b commutes with. b^{1/2^n} is rendered as the n-fold iterate of CFC.sqrt rather than the CFC power, which for an effect is the same element. Proof is the thesis's 56I.20-50 with one local deviation: for p <= p^2 the thesis rewrites p^2 as a double supremum using ad-normal (44VIII) and reads off b^{1/2^k}; ours bounds each generator directly, b^{1/2^k} = b^{1/2^{k+2}} b^{1/2^{k+1}} b^{1/2^{k+2}} <= b^{1/2^{k+2}} p b^{1/2^{k+2}} = sqrt p b^{1/2^{k+1}} sqrt p <= p p, using only monotonicity of conjugation. Same chain, no appeal to ad-normal
column7: left: a local deviation inside the thesis's own chain (56I.20-50), not a different argument. Dead-limb check clean -- ad_normal, the step our version avoids, has five other consumers (A/VN/Basic 2343, 3276, 5505, A/VN/Projections via ad_normal_inf, B/Dils/Stinespring 558), so restoring it here would buy length and nothing else.

column6: well-definedness of ceil for an arbitrary POSITIVE b, in the 59III.1 form 'least projection p with b p = b'. The thesis proves 56I for effects and extends by the rescaling of 59I; ours does the same (exists_normalize), but applies the rescaling even when b is already an effect of norm < 1, which is harmless since 56XIII.2/59III.4 give ceil (lambda b) = ceil b
column7: left: the thesis does the same rescaling (59I); the only deviation is applying it unconditionally, which 56XIII.2 / 59III.4 make harmless.

column6: definition of the ceiling, combining 56I (effects) and the 59I extension to arbitrary positive b, with junk value 0 off the positive cone. Definition, no proof to match. Note that the thesis's warning at 59I that b <= ceil b FAILS for b not <= 1 is not recorded by any declaration
56I main claim for an effect b: ceil b is the least projection above b, as an IsLeast. Content comes from exists_ceil_effect, i.e. the thesis's own construction
56I's formula ceil b = sup_n b^{1/2^n} for an effect b, with b^{1/2^n} as the n-fold CFC.sqrt iterate. The thesis's construction, so the formula is what is actually proved

56I's 'moreover' clause. The thesis states it for an EFFECT b; ours states it for every positive b, which is the generalisation 59III.2 makes anyway. Free strengthening, obtained from the effect case by rescaling. Proof is 56I.30 (induction along the square roots plus 44XIII vna-supremum-commutes)
column7: left-benign: free strengthening from effects to all positive elements, which 59III.2 makes anyway. Not a defect.

auxiliary: ceil (1-b) is a projection. Not a transcription

56VI vna-floor, well-definedness: the greatest projection p with p b = p, for an effect b. Since 2026-08-25 this is the thesis's own construction: p := the infimum of the b^{2^n} (exists_floor_inf, 56VI.70-90), and 56VI.100 for the leastness -- a projection q <= b satisfies q <= b^2 by 55IX projection-below-effect, hence q <= b^{2^n} for every n by induction, hence q <= the infimum
column7: repaired 2026-08-25 (the edit landed in commit bebf4a5 without its record; verified against vn.tex:2419, finished and recorded here). column6: 56VI in full: floor b is the greatest projection below b AND is the infimum of the b^{2^n}. The thesis's 56VI.70-100 argument is transcribed in the tree; since 2026-08-25 its 70-90 half lives in the private exists_floor_inf -- the filtered chain 1 >= b >= b^2 >= b^4 >= ..., its infimum by 43Ia infima-in-vna, commutation via 44XIII, the projection property via ad_normal_inf applied twice -- which vna_floor, exists_floor and vna_floor_comm all read off, and 56VI.100 (55IX plus induction) supplies the greatest-below-b clause

Our proof is now the thesis's own 56VI.80: whatever commutes with b commutes with every b^{2^n} and hence with their infimum (44XIII vna_infimum_commutes, via exists_floor_inf), and that infimum is floor b

56XI part 2 (pa = p iff ap = p iff p <= floor a) as a TFAE. Exercise, no thesis proof. As with part 1 the 'conclude'/'in particular' tail (floor a is the greatest projection p with p = ap, and floor a = a floor a = floor a a) is the p := floor a instance, plus floor_spec

Exercise, no thesis proof

column6: 56XIII part 3, both clauses (floor a = floor (a^2) and ceil a = ceil (a^2)). Exercise, no thesis proof

56XIV: the supremum of a directed set of projections is a projection. Nonemptiness of D is an explicit hypothesis here, which the thesis leaves in its reading of 'directed'. Our proof is 56XIV.150: d p = d by 55IX, (d)_d -> p ultraweakly by 44VI and (d p)_d -> p^2 by 44VII, then uniqueness of the limit -- ours closes the last step with np_separating rather than by naming the ultraweak topology Hausdorff, which is the same fact

56XVI, suprema half: every set of projections has a least upper bound in the poset of projections. Exercise, no thesis proof; ours follows the hint (the set of projections below every projection upper bound is directed, by the binary join ceil (x+y) of 56XIII.2, so 56XIV applies)

56XVI, infima half. Exercise, no thesis proof; ours follows the hint's second half, transporting the supremum along the order anti-isomorphism p -> p^perp
56XVI, the definition of intersection A. Definition

56XVII part 1, ceil (sup D) = union of the ceil d, for a directed set of effects. Nonemptiness is an explicit hypothesis. Exercise, no thesis proof; ours is monotonicity of ceil for one inequality and 44VIII ad_normal for the other
56XVII part 2, floor (inf D) = intersection of the floor d, for a filtered set of effects. Exercise, no thesis proof

56XVII part 3 renders only the last of its four claims. The exercise asks (a) ceil does not preserve filtered infima, (b) floor does not preserve directed suprema, and then concludes (c) that neither is ultraweakly, ultrastrongly NOR norm continuous. Ours states only the norm discontinuity of both maps; (a) and (b) are not stated anywhere in the module, and the ultraweak and ultrastrong discontinuities are not stated either -- and do not follow from the norm one, since coarsening the topology on both source and target changes continuity in both directions (the same witness a_n = (n+1)^{-1} 1 does settle all three, but only the norm case is recorded). The doc comment admits 'We record the norm discontinuity'. Also needs [Nontrivial A], which the thesis leaves implicit. Exercise, no thesis proof

The ultraweak and ultrastrong cases really are proved, not inferred from the norm one. `[Nontrivial A]` is documented as what the thesis leaves implicit.

column6: 56XVIII: the net of finite partial sums of a pairwise orthogonal family of projections converges ultrastrongly to their join, over an arbitrary (possibly uncountable) index type, exactly as printed. Exercise, no thesis proof; ours uses the hint's fact (finite partial sums are projections and are the join of their summands) and then normality of the np-functionals

57I: floor (sqrt a b sqrt a) = floor a intersect floor b. The thesis states the same fact twice ('is the greatest projection below a and b, that is, = floor a cap floor b'); ours states the equation, and the greatest-below-a-and-b form is what the proof establishes en route, so nothing is lost. Our proof is 57I.20-30 step for step: f <= sqrt a b sqrt a <= a, then f b f = f from f c f = f, then f <= b by ad-contraposed, then e <= a and e <= b gives e = e sqrt a b sqrt a

58II floor-difference: p - ceil a = floor (p - a) for a projection p and an effect a <= p. Our proof is 58III: p - ceil a is a projection below p - a by 55XIV, and for q <= p - a the thesis's trick a <= p - q gives ceil a <= p - q

58IV: ceil (pqp) = p cap (p^perp cup q). Our proof is 58V: the De Morgan step p cap (p^perp cup q) = p - p cap q^perp, then p - ceil (pqp) = floor (p - pqp) = floor (p q^perp p) = p cap q^perp by 58II and 57I

59I's extension of the ceiling to arbitrary positive b, as the consistency statement ceil b = ceil (‖b‖^{-1} b). Ours proves it for every positive nonzero b, where 59I only needs it for b not <= 1. Notation, no thesis proof

not a thesis statement: the calculation rule 'b c = 0 implies ceil b c = 0' for positive b, which 59IV and 60VIII need. Proved from the 56I supremum formula plus 44VIII ad_normal

59IV part 2, all four equations (ceil a_+ a = a ceil a_+ = a_+ and ceil a_- a = a ceil a_- = -a_-). Exercise, no thesis proof
the common content of 56XVII.1 and 59V, for a nonempty directed set of positive elements; the two DISP-tagged statements are thin wrappers on it
59V, ceil (sup D) = union of ceil d for a bounded directed set of positive elements, with nonemptiness explicit. Exercise, no thesis proof
auxiliary: supp x <= q gives x q = x, a repackaging of 59VI.1
59VI part 1: the support ceil (a* a) is the least projection p with a p = a. Exercise, no thesis proof

59VI part 4, both clauses (supp (ab) <= supp b and range (ab) <= range a). Exercise, no thesis proof

59VII parts 1 and 2: the range projection of a bounded operator T on a Hilbert space is the projection onto closure (Ran T), and the support projection is the projection onto (Ker T)^perp. A projection is identified here by its set of fixed points rather than by a submodule, which is an equivalent rendering. Exercise, no thesis proof
59VII part 3: for an effect T, floor T is the projection onto the fixed points of T. Exercise, no thesis proof

60I: omega a = 0 iff omega (ceil a) = 0 for positive a and an np-functional. Our proof is 60I.20: rescale to an effect, then Kadison's inequality gives omega (a^{1/2^n}) = 0 by induction and normality of omega turns the 56I supremum into a supremum of scalars. The thesis's extra reduction 'for similar reasons we may assume omega(1) <= 1' is not needed here and is not made
auxiliary: Kadison's inequality in the form 60I uses it, omega(a) = 0 forces omega(sqrt a) = 0

60III: ceil a <= ceil b iff every np-functional killing b kills a. Our proof is 60III.40 in both directions, including the thesis's device of testing ceil b ^perp ceil a ceil b ^perp against the np-functional omega (ceil b ^perp (.) ceil b ^perp)

60V ncp-ceil: ceil (f a) = ceil (f (ceil a)) for an np-map f and positive a. Our proof is 60VI: 60III reduces it to omega(f a) = 0 iff omega(f (ceil a)) = 0, which is 60I for the np-functional omega o f
60VII part 1: ceil (a* b a) = ceil (a* ceil b a) for b >= 0. Exercise, but it says 'deduce from ncp-ceil', and ours is literally 60V applied to the np-map x -> a* x a (normal by 44VIII)
60VII part 2, both clauses (supp (ab) = supp (supp a b) and range (ab) = range (a range b)). Exercise, no thesis proof

60VIII part 1, all three equivalents (cb = 0 iff supp c range b = 0 iff supp c <= (range b)^perp). Exercise, no thesis proof; ours does not use the printed hint (ceil (b* c* c b) = ceil (b* ceil (c* c) b) = 0 via 60VII) but the equivalent route through ceil_mul_eq_zero

The hint's chain is ceil(b* c* c b) = ceil(b* ceil(c*c) b) = 0 by 60VII ceil-fundamental; ours pushes the ceiling through in one step -- c*c b = 0 gives ceil(c*c) b = 0 by `ceil_mul_eq_zero`, and the same on the other side -- so no content of the hint is bypassed.

60IX part 1 (ceil (f (p cup q)) = ceil (f p) cup ceil (f q)). Exercise, no thesis proof; ours follows the printed hint, p cup q = ceil (p/2 + q/2) from 56XIII.2

60IX part 2 (ceil (f (union P)) = union of ceil (f p)) for an arbitrary set of projections. Exercise, no thesis proof; ours uses part 1 and 60V as the exercise directs, through the directed set of projections q with ceil (f q) below the right-hand side
not a separate thesis statement: 60IX.2 specialised to the np-map x -> b* x b, the form used at 68I and 69V
60IX part 3 (there is a greatest projection e with f e = 0). Exercise, no thesis proof

61II ncp-ceill, both inequalities, in the direction the CURRENT vn.tex prints and the 61III proof establishes -- which is also the direction asols' erratum parsec-610.20 ('both inequalities should be reversed') installs, so vn.tex already carries the correction. OUR DOC DEFECT: the doc comment asserts that 'the thesis displays the inequalities in the opposite direction', which is no longer true of vn.tex, and it does not cite the erratum. Our proof is 61III's chain, with the positive constant ‖f(1)‖+1 substituted for ‖f(1)‖^2 to avoid a case split at f = 0, and the second inequality obtained from the first at a*

62I: floor (f a) = floor (f (floor a)) for an ncpsu-map and an effect a. Our proof is 62II step for step: floor (f a) = floor (f (a^2)) from 56XIII.3 and cp-cs, induction to a^{2^n}, then normality carries the 56VI infimum floor a = inf_n a^{2^n} through f. (62II's own proof cites parsec-40.150 where it means 340.140, corrected in asols; a proof-internal typo only)

63I, the definition of the carrier of an np-map. Definition
63I specialised to np-functionals; not a separate thesis statement

63II part 1 (carrier (lambda f) = carrier f for lambda > 0). The scaled map is passed as a second map g with g a = lambda f a for all a, since the positive-map type carries no scalar action here; that is the same statement. Exercise, no thesis proof
63II part 2 (carrier (f+g) = carrier f cup carrier g), with the sum given pointwise as a third map. Exercise, no thesis proof
63II part 3 (carrier f = 1 iff f faithful), faithfulness rendered as 'f a = 0 and a >= 0 imply a = 0'. Exercise, no thesis proof

63II part 4 (for multiplicative f: carrier f = 1 iff f injective). Multiplicativity is a hypothesis on the underlying function rather than a bundled nmiu structure, which is what the exercise assumes. Exercise, no thesis proof
63III part 1 (the carrier of a* (.) a is ceil (a a*), the range projection). Exercise, no thesis proof
63III part 2, for T : H -> K between DIFFERENT Hilbert spaces exactly as the exercise states, with the carrier identified by its fixed-point set. Exercise, no thesis proof

63III part 3 (the carrier of the vector functional on all of B(H) is ketbra x x, for a unit vector x). The exercise's parenthetical warning about restricting to a von Neumann subalgebra is a remark and has no declaration. Exercise, no thesis proof

63IV cp-comprehension, for a positive map between C*-algebras (not von Neumann algebras) and an effect p with f p^perp = 0, all three equations. Our proof is 63V in both paragraphs: the scalar case by Kadison's inequality on (p^perp)^2, then the general case by separating with the states of B

63VI carrier-fundamental. The thesis gives no proof text: it states 63VI as an immediate Corollary of 63IV cp-comprehension, and since 2026-08-21 the proof IS that corollary -- one term, `cp_comprehension f (carrier f hf) (the carrier is a projection, hence an effect) (carrier_spec's f(ceil f ^perp) = 0)`. (Until then it re-ran 63IV's Kadison argument with the np-functionals of B as the separating family instead of the states, about 50 lines, and the stated corollary relation was nowhere exhibited.)
